sentences.en: When I was nine years old, I went off to summer camp for the first time.
sentences.zh: 当我九岁的时候,我第一次去参加夏令营。

sentences.en: And my mother packed me a suitcase full of books, which to me seemed like a perfectly natural thing to do.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈帮我整理好了行李箱， 里面塞满了书，这对于我来说 是一件极为自然的事情。

sentences.en: Because in my family, reading was the primary group activity.
sentences.zh: 因为在我家， 阅读是首要的集体活动。

sentences.en: And this might sound antisocial to you, but for us it was really just a different way of being social.
sentences.zh: 听上去我这一家都不爱社交，但对我们来说 看书也社交的另一种途径。

sentences.en: You have the animal warmth of your family sitting right next to you, but you are also free to go roaming around the adventureland inside your own mind.
sentences.zh: 你可以享受被自己家人围绕的温暖，但你也可以自由地漫游在 思维深处的冒险乐园。

sentences.en: And I had this idea that camp was going to be just like this, but better.
sentences.zh: 我当时以为夏令营就是这样，当然要更好些。

sentences.en: (Laughter) I had a vision of 10 girls sitting in a cabin cozily reading books in their matching nightgowns.
sentences.zh: （笑声）我想象十个女孩坐在一个小屋里，穿着配套的睡裙 惬意地读书。（笑声）

sentences.en: (Laughter) Camp was more like a keg party without any alcohol.
sentences.zh: 事实上，夏令营更像是 没有酒精的派对聚会。

sentences.en: And on the very first day, our counselor gathered us all together and she taught us a cheer that she said we would be doing every day for the rest of the summer to instill camp spirit.
sentences.zh: 在第一天的时候，指导员把我们都集合在一起。她教会了我们一种 在余下夏令营的每一天中都会用到的加油口号，

sentences.en: And it went like this: "R-O-W-D-I-E, that's the way we spell rowdie.
sentences.zh: 来凝聚我们的“夏令营精神”。听上去是这样的：“R-O-W-D-I-E，这是我们拼写“吵闹"的口号！

sentences.en: Rowdie, rowdie, let's get rowdie." (Laughter) Yeah.
sentences.zh: 噪音，喧闹， 我们要变得吵一点！”（笑声）

sentences.en: So I couldn't figure out for the life of me why we were supposed to be so rowdy, or why we had to spell this word incorrectly.
sentences.zh: 对，就是这样。可我怎样也不明白为什么我们需要这么吵闹？为什么我们非要错误地拼写 “Rowdy”?

sentences.en: (Laughter) But I recited a cheer. I recited a cheer along with everybody else.
sentences.zh: （笑声）但我还是和其他伙伴一起 背熟了这个口号。

sentences.en: I did my best. And I just waited for the time that I could go off and read my books.
sentences.zh: 我尽了我最大的努力。我在等待可以捧起 我挚爱的书的那一刻。

sentences.en: But the first time that I took my book out of my suitcase, the coolest girl in the bunk came up to me and she asked me, "Why are you being so mellow?" -- mellow, of course, being the exact opposite of R-O-W-D-I-E.
sentences.zh: 但当我第一次把书从行李箱中拿出来时，宿舍中最酷的那个女孩向我走了过来，并且她问我：“为什么你要这么安静？”安静，当然，是R-O-W-D-I-E

sentences.en: And then the second time I tried it, the counselor came up to me with a concerned expression on her face and she repeated the point about camp spirit and said we should all work very hard to be outgoing.
sentences.zh: “喧闹”的反义词。而当我第二次拿书的时候，指导员满脸忧虑的向我走来，她重复了关于“夏令营精神”的要点，并且说我们都应当努力 去变得外向些。

sentences.en: And so I put my books away, back in their suitcase, and I put them under my bed, and there they stayed for the rest of the summer.
sentences.zh: 于是，我放好我的书，放回了行李箱中，并把箱子塞回了床底，在暑假余下的日子， 书再也没被拿出来过。

sentences.en: And I felt kind of guilty about this. I felt as if the books needed me somehow, and they were calling out to me and I was forsaking them.
sentences.zh: 我对这样做感到挺愧疚的。我感觉这些书是需要我的，它们在呼唤我， 但是我却放弃了它们。

sentences.en: But I did forsake them and I didn't open that suitcase again until I was back home with my family at the end of the summer.
sentences.zh: 我确实放下了它们， 并且我再也没有打开那个箱子直到在暑期结束我回家。

sentences.en: Now, I tell you this story about summer camp.
sentences.zh: 我刚讲的是夏令营的故事，

sentences.en: I could have told you 50 others just like it -- all the times that I got the message that somehow my quiet and introverted style of being was not necessarily the right way to go, that I should be trying to pass as more of an extrovert.
sentences.zh: 我还可以告诉你们50个类似的经历，在这些经历中， 我都反复收到一个信号我的文静和内向的性格 挺不对劲的，我应该努力变成一个外向者的角色。

sentences.en: And I always sensed deep down that this was wrong and that introverts were pretty excellent just as they were.
sentences.zh: 而在我内心深处一直觉得， 这种想法是错误的，内向的人做自己也非常优秀。

sentences.en: But for years I denied this intuition, and so I became a Wall Street lawyer, of all things, instead of the writer that I had always longed to be -- partly because I needed to prove to myself that I could be bold and assertive too.
sentences.zh: 但是多年来 我都否认了这种直觉。我首先成为了华尔街的一名律师，而不是我长久以来 想要成为的一名作家。一部分原因是我想向自己证明 我可以变得勇敢而坚定。

sentences.en: And I was always going off to crowded bars when I really would have preferred to just have a nice dinner with friends.
sentences.zh: 并且我总是去那些热闹的酒吧，虽然我只想和朋友们 吃一顿不错的晚餐。

sentences.en: And I made these self-negating choices so reflexively, that I wasn't even aware that I was making them.
sentences.zh: 我做出了很多自我否认的抉择如条件反射一般，甚至我都没有意识到 我做出了这些决定。

sentences.en: Now this is what many introverts do, and it's our loss for sure, but it is also our colleagues' loss and our communities' loss.
sentences.zh: 这是很多内向的人正在做的事情，这当然是我们的损失，但这同样也是同事们的损失，

sentences.en: And at the risk of sounding grandiose, it is the world's loss.
sentences.zh: 我们所在团队集体的损失。也许听起来有些夸大其词， 这更是世界的损失。

sentences.en: Because when it comes to creativity and to leadership, we need introverts doing what they do best.
sentences.zh: 因为当涉及创造力和领导力的时候，

sentences.en: A third to a half of the population are introverts -- a third to a half.
sentences.zh: 我们需要内向的人发挥长处。世上三分到二分之一的人口都是内向的，

sentences.en: So that's one out of every two or three people you know.
sentences.zh: 三分之一到二分之一。这意味着你认识的每两到三个人中 就有一个内向的。

sentences.en: So even if you're an extrovert yourself, I'm talking about your coworkers and your spouses and your children and the person sitting next to you right now -- all of them subject to this bias that is pretty deep and real in our society.
sentences.zh: 即使你自己是一个外向的人，我正在说你的同事和你的配偶和你的孩子还有正坐在你旁边的那个家伙，他们都要屈从于这样的偏见，一种在社会中扎根的偏见。

sentences.en: We all internalize it from a very early age without even having a language for what we're doing.
sentences.zh: 我们从很小的时候就 内化了这种偏见甚至都不知道是怎么一回事。

sentences.en: Now, to see the bias clearly, you need to understand what introversion is.
sentences.zh: 让我们来清楚地看待这种偏见，我们需要真正了解“内向”到底指什么。

sentences.en: It's different from being shy. Shyness is about fear of social judgment.
sentences.zh: 它和害羞是不同的。害羞是对于社会眼光的恐惧，

sentences.en: Introversion is more about, how do you respond to stimulation, including social stimulation.
sentences.zh: 内向更多的是你怎样对于刺激作出回应，

sentences.en: So extroverts really crave large amounts of stimulation, whereas introverts feel at their most alive and their most switched-on and their most capable when they're in quieter, more low-key environments.
sentences.zh: 包括来自社会的刺激。外向的人是很渴求大量刺激，反之内向者则是相反的，他们最敏锐、最充足、最具有能力是当他们处于更安静的， 更低调的环境中。

sentences.en: Not all the time -- these things aren't absolute -- but a lot of the time.
sentences.zh: 并不是所有时候， 这些事情不是绝对的，在大多数情况下就是这样。

sentences.en: So the key then to maximizing our talents is for us all to put ourselves in the zone of stimulation that is right for us.
sentences.zh: 关键在于若想将我们这些内向者的天赋最大化，我们需要将自己 置身于适合我们的激励区域中。

sentences.en: But now here's where the bias comes in. Our most important institutions, our schools and our workplaces, they are designed mostly for extroverts and for extroverts' need for lots of stimulation.
sentences.zh: 但偏见会来捣乱，我们最重要的一些体系：学校和工作单位它们都是为性格外向者设计的，并且有适合他们需要的刺激和鼓励。

sentences.en: And also we have this belief system right now that I call the new groupthink, which holds that all creativity and all productivity comes from a very oddly gregarious place.
sentences.zh: 我们现在有一种思维惯例，我称它为新型的“团队思考”，这种思维觉得创造力和生产力都来源于社交场合。

sentences.en: So if you picture the typical classroom nowadays: When I was going to school, we sat in rows.
sentences.zh: 想象一下如今典型教室情形。在我上学的时候， 学生一排排地坐着。

sentences.en: We sat in rows of desks like this, and we did most of our work pretty autonomously.
sentences.zh: 坐在一排排的课桌后，学生大多会独自完成自己的作业。

sentences.en: But nowadays, your typical classroom has pods of desks -- four or five or six or seven kids all facing each other.
sentences.zh: 但如今，一个典型的教室中 有的是一组组课桌——四、五个，六、七个孩子 面对面坐在一起。

sentences.en: And kids are working in countless group assignments.
sentences.zh: 孩子们要完成无数个小组任务。

sentences.en: Even in subjects like math and creative writing, which you think would depend on solo flights of thought, kids are now expected to act as committee members.
sentences.zh: 甚至在数学和创意写作，这些本可以独立完成的科目，现在孩子们被当成小组会的成员。

sentences.en: And for the kids who prefer to go off by themselves or just to work alone, those kids are seen as outliers often or, worse, as problem cases.
sentences.zh: 对于那些喜欢独处， 或者独自学习的孩子来说他们常常被视为局外人，

sentences.en: And the vast majority of teachers reports believing that the ideal student is an extrovert as opposed to an introvert, even though introverts actually get better grades and are more knowledgeable, according to research.
sentences.zh: 更糟的情况下， 他们会被视为问题孩子。很大一部分老师的报告中都相信最理想的学生应是外向的 而非内向的。事实上，内向的学生有着更好的成绩更加博学多识，有研究报告显示。（笑声）

sentences.en: (Laughter) Okay, same thing is true in our workplaces.
sentences.zh: 同样的事情也发生在工作场合。

sentences.en: Now, most of us work in open plan offices, without walls, where we are subject to the constant noise and gaze of our coworkers.
sentences.zh: 如今，大多数人都在 开敞式办公室里工作，没有隔墙，我们在不断的噪音中工作 也暴露于同事的目光下。

sentences.en: And when it comes to leadership, introverts are routinely passed over for leadership positions, even though introverts tend to be very careful, much less likely to take outsize risks -- which is something we might all favor nowadays.
sentences.zh: 而当谈及领袖气质的时候，在选择领导时， 内向的人总会被忽视，尽管内向的人通常小心仔细，很少去冒险 ——这些都是我们所称赞的气质。

sentences.en: And interesting research by Adam Grant at the Wharton School has found that introverted leaders often deliver better outcomes than extroverts do, because when they are managing proactive employees, they're much more likely to let those employees run with their ideas,
sentences.zh: 沃顿商学院的亚当·格兰特教授 做了一项很有意思的研究表明内向的领导们相较外向领导，更能取得高业绩。因为当他们管理主动积极的雇员时他们更倾向于 让有主见的雇员自由发挥，

sentences.en: whereas an extrovert can, quite unwittingly, get so excited about things that they're putting their own stamp on things, and other people's ideas might not as easily then bubble up to the surface.
sentences.zh: 反之，外向的领导就可能， 当然是不经意的，容易对事物反应过度，容易以自己的想法独大导致他人的想法很难出头。

sentences.en: Now in fact, some of our transformative leaders in history have been introverts.
sentences.zh: 事实上，历史上一些变革型领袖 都是内向的人。

sentences.en: I'll give you some examples. Eleanor Roosevelt, Rosa Parks, Gandhi -- all these people described themselves as quiet and soft-spoken and even shy.
sentences.zh: 举一些例子。埃莉诺·罗斯福、罗沙·帕克斯、 甘地 ——这些人都把自己描述成内向， 轻言细语甚至是害羞的人。

sentences.en: And they all took the spotlight, even though every bone in their bodies was telling them not to.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然站在了聚光灯下即使这样做会让他们浑身感到不适。

sentences.en: And this turns out to have a special power all its own, because people could feel that these leaders were at the helm not because they enjoyed directing others and not out of the pleasure of being looked at; they were there because they had no choice,
sentences.zh: 这成为了一种独特的力量，因为人们都会感觉到 这些领袖成为掌舵者并不是因为他们喜欢指挥别人，抑或是享受众人目光的聚焦，

sentences.en: because they were driven to do what they thought was right.
sentences.zh: 而是因为他们没有选择因为他们坚信的正义 驱使着他们。

sentences.en: Now I think at this point it's important for me to say that I actually love extroverts.
sentences.zh: 我在这里必须提一下，

sentences.en: I always like to say some of my best friends are extroverts, including my beloved husband.
sentences.zh: 我非常喜爱外向的人。我总是喜欢说我最好的朋友 都是外向的人，包括我亲爱的丈夫。

sentences.en: And we all fall at different points, of course, along the introvert/extrovert spectrum.
sentences.zh: 当然，在内向者到外向者 这一范围中，人们都有各自的不同。

sentences.en: Even Carl Jung, the psychologist who first popularized these terms, said that there's no such thing as a pure introvert or a pure extrovert.
sentences.zh: 卡尔·荣格， 这个推广这些术语的心理学家，说过世上绝没有一个纯粹的内向或外向的人。

sentences.en: He said that such a man would be in a lunatic asylum, if he existed at all.
sentences.zh: 他说那人若真存在 一定会在精神病院里。

sentences.en: And some people fall smack in the middle of the introvert/extrovert spectrum, and we call these people ambiverts.
sentences.zh: 还有一些人处在 在内向与外向中间。我们称这些人为“中向性格者”。

sentences.en: And I often think that they have the best of all worlds.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们幸运地取得了完美的平衡。

sentences.en: But many of us do recognize ourselves as one type or the other.
sentences.zh: 但是我们中的大多数会认为 自己属于内向或外向的其中一类。

sentences.en: And what I'm saying is that culturally, we need a much better balance.
sentences.zh: 从文化上讲， 我们需要一种更好的平衡。

sentences.en: We need more of a yin and yang between these two types.
sentences.zh: 我们需要更多的阴阳平衡在这两种类型的人之间。

sentences.en: This is especially important when it comes to creativity and to productivity, because when psychologists look at the lives of the most creative people, what they find are people who are very good at exchanging ideas
sentences.zh: 这点是极为重要的，特别是涉及创造力和生产力，因为当心理学家们研究 那些最有创造力的人时他们寻找到的

sentences.en: and advancing ideas, but who also have a serious streak of introversion in them.
sentences.zh: 是擅长交流想法、提出想法的人，但同时也有着显著的内向倾向。

sentences.en: And this is because solitude is a crucial ingredient often to creativity.
sentences.zh: 这是因为独处是激发创造力的重要因素。

sentences.en: So Darwin, he took long walks alone in the woods and emphatically turned down dinner-party invitations.
sentences.zh: 比如说，达尔文会一个人漫步在小树林里，并且断然拒绝晚餐派对的邀约。

sentences.en: Theodor Geisel, better known as Dr. Seuss, he dreamed up many of his amazing creations in a lonely bell tower office that he had in the back of his house in La Jolla, California.
sentences.zh: 西奥多·盖索， 就是大家所熟知的苏斯博士，他的许多梦幻作品都创作于他在加州拉霍亚市房子后的一座孤独的塔形办公室中。

sentences.en: And he was actually afraid to meet the young children who read his books for fear that they were expecting him this kind of jolly Santa Claus-like figure and would be disappointed with his more reserved persona.
sentences.zh: 而且，他还不太敢去与他的小书迷们见面，害怕孩子们会期待 他是像圣诞老人一般的可爱形象，而会对他实际含蓄的性格感到失望。

sentences.en: Steve Wozniak invented the first Apple computer sitting alone in his cubicle in Hewlett-Packard where he was working at the time.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫·沃兹尼亚克 发明第一台苹果电脑时也是一个人独自坐在惠普公司的一个小方间中。

sentences.en: And he says that he never would have become such an expert in the first place had he not been too introverted to leave the house when he was growing up.
sentences.zh: 他说他成为电脑方面专家也是因为成长过程中过于内向 不敢出门。

sentences.en: Now, of course, this does not mean that we should all stop collaborating -- and case in point, is Steve Wozniak famously coming together with Steve Jobs to start Apple Computer -- but it does mean that solitude matters
sentences.zh: 当然了这并不意味着我们都应该停止团队合作。你看，史蒂夫·沃兹尼亚克和 史蒂夫·乔布斯的强强联手创建了苹果公司。但这证明了独处的重要性，

sentences.en: and that for some people it is the air that they breathe.
sentences.zh: 对有些人来说,那是他们呼吸的空气。

sentences.en: And in fact, we have known for centuries about the transcendent power of solitude.
sentences.zh: 并且对于一些人来说 独处就像赖以呼吸生存的空气。我们已经明了独处的卓越力量很久了。

sentences.en: It's only recently that we've strangely begun to forget it.
sentences.zh: 只是到了最近，非常奇怪， 我们开始遗忘它了。

sentences.en: If you look at most of the world's major religions, you will find seekers -- Moses, Jesus, Buddha, Muhammad -- seekers who are going off by themselves alone to the wilderness, where they then have profound epiphanies and revelations
sentences.zh: 如果你看看世界上主要的宗教你会发现探寻者：摩西，耶稣，佛祖，穆罕默德他们在旷野中独处并思索，在那儿，他们得到了深刻的顿悟，

sentences.en: that they then bring back to the rest of the community.
sentences.zh: 并将这些思想带回并贡献给社会。

sentences.en: So, no wilderness, no revelations. This is no surprise, though, if you look at the insights of contemporary psychology.
sentences.zh: 没有旷原，没有启示尽管这并不令人惊讶如果你注意到现代心理学的思想理论

sentences.en: It turns out that we can't even be in a group of people without instinctively mirroring, mimicking their opinions.
sentences.zh: 它反映出来我们甚至不能和一组人待在一起而不去本能地模仿他们的意见与想法

sentences.en: Even about seemingly personal and visceral things like who you're attracted to, you will start aping the beliefs of the people around you without even realizing that that's what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 甚至是看上去私人的，发自内心的事情像是你被谁所吸引你会开始模仿你周围的人的信仰甚至都觉察不到你自己在做什么

sentences.en: And groups famously follow the opinions of the most dominant or charismatic person in the room, even though there's zero correlation between being the best talker and having the best ideas -- I mean zero.
sentences.zh: 还曾跟随群体的意见跟随着房间里最具有统治力的，最有领袖气质的人的思路虽然这真的没什么关系在成为一个卓越的演讲家还是拥有最好的主意之间--

sentences.en: So -- (Laughter) You might be following the person with the best ideas, but you might not.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是“零相关”那么...（笑声）你们或许会跟随有最好头脑的人

sentences.en: And do you really want to leave it up to chance?
sentences.zh: 但是你们也许不会

sentences.en: Much better for everybody to go off by themselves, generate their own ideas freed from the distortions of group dynamics, and then come together as a team to talk them through in a well-managed environment and take it from there.
sentences.zh: 可你们真的想把这机会扔掉吗？如果每个人都自己行动或许好得多发掘他们自己的想法没有群体动力学的曲解接着来到一起组成一个团队在一个良好管理的环境中互相交流

sentences.en: Now if all this is true, then why are we getting it so wrong?
sentences.zh: 并且在那里学习别的思想如果说现在这一切都是真的

sentences.en: Why are we setting up our schools this way, and our workplaces?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么我们还得到这样错误的结论？

sentences.en: And why are we making these introverts feel so guilty about wanting to just go off by themselves some of the time?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们要这样创立我们的学校，还有我们的工作单位？为什么我们要让这些内向的人觉得那么愧疚对于他们只是想要离开，一个人独处一段时间的事实？

sentences.en: One answer lies deep in our cultural history.
sentences.zh: 有一个答案在我们的文化史中埋藏已久

sentences.en: Western societies, and in particular the U.S., have always favored the man of action over the "man" of contemplation.
sentences.zh: 西方社会特别是在美国总是偏爱有行动的人而不是有深刻思考的人

sentences.en: But in America's early days, we lived in what historians call a culture of character, where we still, at that point, valued people for their inner selves and their moral rectitude.
sentences.zh: 有深刻思考的“人”但是在美国早期的时候我们生活在一个被历史学家称作“性格特征”的文化那时我们仍然，在这点上，判断人们的价值从人们的内涵和道义正直

sentences.en: And if you look at the self-help books from this era, they all had titles with things like "Character, the Grandest Thing in the World."
sentences.zh: 而且如果你看一看这个时代关于自立的书籍的话它们都有这样一种标题：

sentences.en: And they featured role models like Abraham Lincoln, who was praised for being modest and unassuming.
sentences.zh: “性格”，世界上最伟大的事物并且它们以亚伯拉罕·林肯这样的为标榜

sentences.en: Ralph Waldo Emerson called him "A man who does not offend by superiority."
sentences.zh: 一个被形容为谦虚低调的男人拉尔夫·瓦尔多·爱默生称他是“一个以‘优越’二字形容都不为过的人”

sentences.en: But then we hit the 20th century, and we entered a new culture that historians call the culture of personality.
sentences.zh: 但是接着我们来到了二十世纪并且我们融入了一种新的文化一种被历史学家称作“个性”的文化

sentences.en: What happened is we had evolved an agricultural economy to a world of big business.
sentences.zh: 所发生的改变就是我们从农业经济发展为一个大商业经济的世界

sentences.en: And so suddenly people are moving from small towns to the cities.
sentences.zh: 而且人们突然开始搬迁从小的城镇搬向城市

sentences.en: And instead of working alongside people they've known all their lives, now they are having to prove themselves in a crowd of strangers.
sentences.zh: 并且一改他们之前的在生活中和所熟识的人们一起工作的方式现在他们在一群陌生人中间有必要去证明自己

sentences.en: So, quite understandably, qualities like magnetism and charisma suddenly come to seem really important.
sentences.zh: 这样做是非常可以理解的像领袖气质和个人魅力这样的品质突然间似乎变得极为重要

sentences.en: And sure enough, the self-help books change to meet these new needs and they start to have names like "How to Win Friends and Influence People."
sentences.zh: 那么可以肯定的是，自助自立的书的内容变更了以适应这些新的需求并且它们开始拥有名称像是《如何赢得朋友和影响他人》（戴尔・卡耐基所著《人性的弱点》）

sentences.en: And they feature as their role models really great salesmen.
sentences.zh: 他们的特点是做自己的榜样不得不说确实是好的推销员

sentences.en: So that's the world we're living in today.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们今天生活的世界

sentences.en: That's our cultural inheritance. Now none of this is to say that social skills are unimportant, and I'm also not calling for the abolishing of teamwork at all.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的文化遗产现在没有谁能够说社交技能是不重要的并且我也不是想呼吁

sentences.en: The same religions who send their sages off to lonely mountain tops also teach us love and trust.
sentences.zh: 大家废除团队合作模式但仍是相同的宗教，却把他们的圣人送到了孤独的山顶上

sentences.en: And the problems that we are facing today in fields like science and in economics are so vast and so complex that we are going to need armies of people coming together to solve them working together.
sentences.zh: 仍然教导我们爱与信任还有我们今天所要面对的问题像是在科学和经济领域是如此的巨大和复杂以至于我们需要人们强有力地团结起来共同解决这些问题

sentences.en: But I am saying that the more freedom that we give introverts to be themselves, the more likely that they are to come up with their own unique solutions to these problems.
sentences.zh: 但是我想说，越给内向者自由让他们做自己他们就做得越好去想出他们独特的关于问题的解决办法

sentences.en: So now I'd like to share with you what's in my suitcase today.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我很高兴同你们分享我手提箱中的东西

sentences.en: Guess what? Books. I have a suitcase full of books.
sentences.zh: 猜猜是什么？书

sentences.en: Here's Margaret Atwood, "Cat's Eye." Here's a novel by Milan Kundera.
sentences.zh: 我有一个手提箱里面装满了书这是玛格丽特·阿特伍德的《猫的眼睛》

sentences.en: And here's "The Guide for the Perplexed" by Maimonides.
sentences.zh: 这是一本米兰·昆德拉的书这是一本《迷途指津》

sentences.en: But these are not exactly my books. I brought these books with me because they were written by my grandfather's favorite authors.
sentences.zh: 是迈蒙尼德写的但这些实际上都不是我的书我还是带着它们，陪伴着我因为它们都是我祖父最喜爱的作家所写

sentences.en: My grandfather was a rabbi and he was a widower who lived alone in a small apartment in Brooklyn that was my favorite place in the world when I was growing up, partly because it was filled with his very gentle, very courtly presence
sentences.zh: 我的祖父是一名犹太教祭司他独身一人在布鲁克林的一间小公寓中居住那里是我从小到大在这个世界上最喜爱的地方部分原因是他有着非常温和亲切的，温文尔雅的举止

sentences.en: and partly because it was filled with books.
sentences.zh: 部分是因为里面装满了书

sentences.en: I mean literally every table, every chair in this apartment had yielded its original function to now serve as a surface for swaying stacks of books.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是那里充满了书我的意思是，毫不夸张地说，公寓中的每张桌子，每张椅子都充分应用着它原有的功能就是现在作为承载一大堆都在摇曳的书的表面

sentences.en: Just like the rest of my family, my grandfather's favorite thing to do in the whole world was to read.
sentences.zh: 就像我其他的家庭成员一样我祖父在这个世界上最喜欢做的事情就是阅读

sentences.en: But he also loved his congregation, and you could feel this love in the sermons that he gave every week for the 62 years that he was a rabbi.
sentences.zh: 但是他同样也热爱他的宗教并且你们可以从他的讲述中感觉到他这种爱这62年来每周他都作为一名犹太教的祭司

sentences.en: He would takes the fruits of each week's reading and he would weave these intricate tapestries of ancient and humanist thought.
sentences.zh: 他会从每周的阅读中汲取养分并且他会编织这些错综复杂的古代和人文主义的思想的挂毯

sentences.en: And people would come from all over to hear him speak.
sentences.zh: 并且人们会从各个地方前来

sentences.en: But here's the thing about my grandfather.
sentences.zh: 听他的讲话但是有这么一件关于我祖父的事情

sentences.en: Underneath this ceremonial role, he was really modest and really introverted -- so much so that when he delivered these sermons, he had trouble making eye contact with the very same congregation that he had been speaking to for 62 years.
sentences.zh: 在这个正式的角色下隐藏着他是一个非常谦虚的非常内向的人是那么的谦虚内向以至于当他在向人们讲述的时候他都不敢有视线上的接触和同样的教堂会众他已经发言有62年了

sentences.en: And even away from the podium, when you called him to say hello, he would often end the conversation prematurely for fear that he was taking up too much of your time.
sentences.zh: 甚至都还远离领奖台当你们让他说“你好”的时候他总会提早结束这对话担心他会占用你太多的时间

sentences.en: But when he died at the age of 94, the police had to close down the streets of his neighborhood to accommodate the crowd of people who came out to mourn him.
sentences.zh: 但是当他94岁去世的时候警察们需要封锁他所居住的街道邻里来容纳拥挤的人们前来哀悼他的人们

sentences.en: And so these days I try to learn from my grandfather's example in my own way.
sentences.zh: 这些天来我都试着从我祖父的事例中学习以我自己的方式

sentences.en: So I just published a book about introversion, and it took me about seven years to write.
sentences.zh: 所以我就出版了一本关于内向性格的书它花了我7年的时间完成它

sentences.en: And for me, that seven years was like total bliss, because I was reading, I was writing, I was thinking, I was researching.
sentences.zh: 而对我来说，这七年像是一种极大的喜悦因为我在阅读，我在写作我在思考，我在探寻

sentences.en: It was my version of my grandfather's hours of the day alone in his library.
sentences.zh: 这是我的版本对于爷爷一天中几个小时都要独自待在图书馆这件事

sentences.en: But now all of a sudden my job is very different, and my job is to be out here talking about it, talking about introversion.
sentences.zh: 但是现在突然间我的工作变得很不同了我的工作变成了站在这里讲述它讲述内向的性格

sentences.en: (Laughter) And that's a lot harder for me, because as honored as I am to be here with all of you right now, this is not my natural milieu.
sentences.zh: （笑声）而且这对于我来说是有一点困难的因为我很荣幸在现在被你们所有人所倾听这可不是我自然的文化背景

sentences.en: So I prepared for moments like these as best I could.
sentences.zh: 所以我准备了一会就像这样

sentences.en: I spent the last year practicing public speaking every chance I could get.
sentences.zh: 以我所能做到的最好的方式我花了最近一年的时间练习在公共场合发言在我能得到的每一个机会中

sentences.en: And I call this my "year of speaking dangerously."
sentences.zh: 我把这一年称作我的“危险地发言的一年”

sentences.en: (Laughter) And that actually helped a lot.
sentences.zh: （笑声）而且它的确帮了我很大的忙

sentences.en: But I'll tell you, what helps even more is my sense, my belief, my hope that when it comes to our attitudes to introversion and to quiet and to solitude, we truly are poised on the brink on dramatic change.
sentences.zh: 但是我要告诉你们一个帮我更大的忙的事情那就是我的感觉，我的信仰，我的希望当谈及我们态度的时候对于内向性格的，对于安静，对于独处的态度时我们确实是在急剧变化的边缘上保持微妙的平衡

sentences.en: I mean, we are. And so I am going to leave you now with three calls for action for those who share this vision.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们在保持平衡现在我将要给你们留下一些东西三件对于你们的行动有帮助的事情献给那些观看我的演讲的人

sentences.en: Number one: Stop the madness for constant group work.
sentences.zh: 第一：停止对于经常要团队协作的执迷与疯狂

sentences.en: Just stop it. (Laughter) Thank you. (Applause) And I want to be clear about what I'm saying, because I deeply believe our offices
sentences.zh: 停止它就好了（笑声）谢谢你们（掌声）我想让我所说的事情变得清晰一些因为我对于我们的办公深信不疑

sentences.en: should be encouraging casual, chatty cafe-style types of interactions -- you know, the kind where people come together and serendipitously have an exchange of ideas.
sentences.zh: 应该鼓励它们那种休闲随意的，聊天似的咖啡厅式的相互作用--你们知道的，道不同不相为谋，人们聚到一起并且互相交换着宝贵的意见

sentences.en: That is great. It's great for introverts and it's great for extroverts.
sentences.zh: 这是很棒的这对于内向者很好，同样对于外向者也好

sentences.en: But we need much more privacy and much more freedom and much more autonomy at work.
sentences.zh: 但是我们需要更多的隐私和更多的自由还有更多对于我们本身工作的自主权

sentences.en: School, same thing. We need to be teaching kids to work together, for sure, but we also need to be teaching them how to work on their own.
sentences.zh: 对于学校，也是同样的。我们当然需要教会孩子们要一起学习工作但是我们同样需要教会孩子们怎么样独立完成任务

sentences.en: This is especially important for extroverted children too.
sentences.zh: 这对于外向的孩子们来说同样是极为重要的

sentences.en: They need to work on their own because that is where deep thought comes from in part.
sentences.zh: 他们需要独立完成工作因为从某种程度上，这是他们深刻思考的来源

sentences.en: Okay, number two: Go to the wilderness. Be like Buddha, have your own revelations.
sentences.zh: 好了，第二个：去到野外（打开思维）就像佛祖一样，拥有你们自己对于事物的揭示启迪

sentences.en: I'm not saying that we all have to now go off and build our own cabins in the woods and never talk to each other again, but I am saying that we could all stand to unplug and get inside our own heads a little more often.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说我们都要跑去小树林里建造我们自己的小屋并且之后就永远不和别人说话了但是我要说我们都可以坚持去去除一些障碍物然后深入我们自己的大脑思想时不时得再深入一点

sentences.en: Number three: Take a good look at what's inside your own suitcase and why you put it there.
sentences.zh: 第三点：好好看一眼你的旅行箱内有什么东西

sentences.en: So extroverts, maybe your suitcases are also full of books.
sentences.zh: 还有你为什么把它放进去所以外向者们也许你们的箱子内同样堆满了书

sentences.en: Or maybe they're full of champagne glasses or skydiving equipment.
sentences.zh: 或者它们装满了香槟的玻璃酒杯或者是跳伞运动的设备

sentences.en: Whatever it is, I hope you take these things out every chance you get and grace us with your energy and your joy.
sentences.zh: 不管它是什么，我希望每当你们有机会你们就把它拿出来用你的能量和你的快乐让我们感受到美和享受

sentences.en: But introverts, you being you, you probably have the impulse to guard very carefully what's inside your own suitcase.
sentences.zh: 但是内向者们，你们作为内向者你们很可能有仔细保护一切的冲动在你箱子里的东西

sentences.en: And that's okay. But occasionally, just occasionally, I hope you will open up your suitcases for other people to see, because the world needs you and it needs the things you carry.
sentences.zh: 这没有问题但是偶尔地，只是说偶尔地我希望你们可以打开你们的手提箱，让别人看一看因为这个世界需要你们，同样需要你们身上所携带的你们特有的事物

sentences.en: So I wish you the best of all possible journeys and the courage to speak softly.
sentences.zh: 所以对于你们即将走上的所有旅程，我都给予你们我最美好的祝愿还有温柔地说话的勇气

sentences.en: Thank you very much. (Applause) Thank you. Thank you.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你们（掌声）谢谢。谢谢

sentences.en: (Applause)
sentences.zh: （掌声）
